questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate antonym of the underlined word.

The good death means accepting death as __inevitable__, and not fighting it when the time comes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"inevitable"** means something that is certain to happen and cannot be avoided. (अनिवार्य)

 
 
• **Example:** Aging is an **inevitable** process that everyone must go through.
 
 
 
• **"Avoidable"** refers to something that can be prevented or kept away from happening. (परिहार्य)
 
 
• **Example:** Many health issues are** avoidable** through proper diet and exercise.
 
 

Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'inevitable'** is **'avoidable'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Imminent** (आसन्न): Something that is about to happen very soon.

 
 
• **Example:** The dark clouds suggest that a storm is imminent.
 
 
 
• **Assured** (आश्वस्त): Something that is guaranteed or certain.
 
 
• **Example:** With his qualifications, a job offer was assured.
 
 
 
• **Fixed** (स्थिर): Something that is securely placed or firmly established.
 
 
• **Example:** The date for the meeting is fixed and cannot be changed.

questions.question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The deer __eat all__ the lettuce in the garden.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The sentence is in the past tense, so the verb should also be in the past tense.
 
• "Eat" is the present tense form of the verb, which is incorrect in this context.
 
• The correct past tense form of "eat" is** "ate".**
 
• Thus, "ate all the lettuce" is the correct phrase.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The deer **ate **all the lettuce in the garden."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Option 2: "had eat all"** – This is grammatically incorrect because "eat" should be in the past participle form "eaten".
 
• **Option 3: "eaten all"** – This is incorrect without an auxiliary verb like "have" or "had" before it.
 
• **Option 4: No improvement** – This is incorrect because "eat" is in the present tense.
